tagline: The back way from Greensboro to the game in Chapel Hill.
intro: From I-85 at Greensboro, Alamance Church Road heads south and Greensboro-Chapel Hill Road carries the byway on, about 42 miles in all, past small dairy farms, creeks and ponds, through Snow Camp and into Carrboro. Most of it is a designated bicycle route, so bicycles are part of the traffic.

The name comes from the Triad fans who drove this way to football games at the university in Chapel Hill. At the NC 62 crossing a side trip of about 4.5 miles east along NC 62 leads to the Alamance battlefield, where Governor Tryon's militia beat the Regulators in 1771.

moments.title: Snow Camp
moments.text: Pennsylvania hunters are said to have camped here in a snowfall, and after Guilford Courthouse Cornwallis briefly took over the Quaker Simon Dixon's house and gristmill for quarters.

moments.title: Eli Whitney
moments.text: A crossroads named for the inventor of the cotton gin, with no tie to him beyond the cotton gin that once stood here.

moments.title: Carrboro
moments.text: The road ends in Carrboro, which grew up around a rail spur that state law kept at least a mile from the university, to guard against damage to student morals and habits of study.
